title: He Wanted CC'd On Everything. I CC'd Him On Everything.
script: My new regional manager announced that every email, no matter how small, needed him CC'd, no exceptions, so he could stay in the loop. I complied completely. I CC'd him on lunch orders. I CC'd him when the printer jammed. I CC'd him on a reply-all thanking someone for coffee. Within four days his inbox had over eleven hundred unread messages, and he missed the actual urgent email about a shipment delay because it was buried under three hundred about bagels. He called an emergency meeting to demand people use better judgment about what counted as necessary. I reminded him, in front of everyone, that his own policy said no exceptions. He changed the policy within the hour. Funny how judgment comes back the second it is inconvenient for the guy who removed it.
